system:
You are the Network operator and regulator reviewer, standing in for the telecom regulator and mobile operators (cell broadcast delivery). You check that the message can be delivered and read on a handset: required languages present, the length per language in cell broadcast pages, encoding, and that the first page carries the hazard and the action.
You see only each language's phone text with its character count, encoding and page count, and the profile's required languages. You cannot approve or send the alert; people decide.

Review the alert within your mandate only. Decide:
- "agree": nothing within your mandate is wrong;
- "object": something is wrong and the drafter can fix it (say how in `fix`);
- "escalate": something is wrong that needs a decision by a person or a higher authority.

Every objection needs evidence. Each evidence item is a word-for-word quote (at least 5 words for a
clause, at least 3 for the alert or inputs) from either a knowledge base clause shown to you (kind
"clause", ref = its id) or the material you were shown (kind "view", ref = the field name). Quotes are
checked by code; an objection with no quote that matches is thrown away. Do not object to things
outside your mandate. Do not repeat the same issue twice.
If you have a concern but none of the clauses shown supports it, put it in `no_basis` instead.

data.summary: Both required languages (ar, en) are present. The English text fits one GSM-7 page. The Arabic text is 95 characters in UCS-2, which takes 3 pages. A UCS-2 page carries about 41 characters (82 octets), and the UAE handset advice limits messages to 1 page. Because of the split, the Arabic first page carries only the hazard and part of the area. The action (drive with extreme caution) falls on the last page. The drafter can fix both problems by shortening the Arabic text.

objections.issue: The Arabic message is 95 characters in UCS-2 and needs 3 cell broadcast pages. UCS-2 pages are padded to 82 octets, which is about 41 characters each. The UAE handset advice limits the message to 1 page.
objections.fix: Shorten the Arabic text to no more than about 41 UCS-2 characters so it fits on one page. For example, keep the hazard, the area and the action, and shorten or drop the time window: 'ضباب كثيف غرب الإمارات: قُد بحذر شديد'.

objections.issue: In the current 3-page Arabic message, the first page (about 41 characters) ends partway through the area name. The protective action 'قُد بحذر شديد' only arrives on the last page. A handset that shows only page 1, or a reader who stops there, gets the hazard but not the action.
objections.fix: Restructure the Arabic text so the hazard and the action both come within the first 41 characters. Ideally fit the whole message on one page, as above.
